edition_notes: French-language rulebook (Règles) by Antoine Bauza, illustrated by Miguel Coimbra, published by Repos Production, © 2012.

items.rule: For all three Age decks, return to the box the cards whose player-count marking (3+, 4+, 5+, 6+, 7+) exceeds the number of players; keep cards marked up to the actual player count.
For the Age III deck, set aside the 10 Guild (purple) cards, randomly and secretly keep only (number of players + 2) of them, and shuffle them into the Age III deck.

Shuffle the 7 Wonder cards face down and deal one to each player; the card and its orientation determine the Wonder board and side (A or B) used. Players may instead choose boards by common agreement; side A is recommended for first games.
Each player starts with 3 coins of value 1 placed on their board; the remaining coins form the bank. Conflict tokens form a reserve next to the coins.
Each board shows the resource its city produces from the start of the game (top left of the board).
A game is played over 3 Ages (I, then II, then III), each using its own deck. At the start of each Age every player receives a hand of 7 random cards from that Age's deck.
Each Age has 6 turns; in each turn all players simultaneously choose one card from their hand, placing it face down, and then reveal and perform their action simultaneously.
With the chosen card a player does one of three actions: (a) build the building, (b) build a stage of their Wonder, or (c) discard the card to take 3 coins from the bank.
After the action, each player passes the remaining hand to a neighbour: Age I to the left (clockwise), Age II to the right (counter-clockwise), Age III to the left (clockwise).
On the sixth turn of each Age players hold 2 cards; they play one normally and discard the other face down, without gaining 3 coins for it.
Building cost: some cards are free, some cost coins (paid to the bank that turn), most cost resources. A player must produce the required resources and/or buy them from the two neighbouring cities.
Resources are not spent when building; a city's production can be used every turn all game, and cards in play are never discarded.
Free construction (chaining): if the player already built the building named on the card's cost line during the previous Age, they can build the card for free.
A player can never build two identical buildings (same name).

Building a Wonder stage: pay the cost shown on the Wonder board (not the card's cost) and slide the chosen card face down half under the board as a marker; the card has no other effect and is not a building.
Wonder stages must be built in order from left to right, each only once per game; stages are not tied to Ages, several can be built in one Age, and building the Wonder is not mandatory.

Discarding for coins: the discarded card goes face down in the centre discard pile and the player takes 3 coins from the bank. A player who can build neither the building nor a stage must discard this way.

Trade: a player can buy resources from the left and right neighbours' Wonder-board resource, brown cards and grey cards, paying 2 coins per resource to that neighbour. Resources from yellow cards and Wonder stages cannot be bought.

Trade details: players cannot refuse to trade; selling a resource does not stop the owner using it the same turn; bought resources only count the turn they are bought; the buyer can split purchases between neighbours and chooses the supplier if both have it.
Coins needed for trade must be held at the start of the turn; coins earned from trade that turn can only be spent from the next turn.

Some yellow buildings reduce the price of purchased resources from 2 to 1 coin, starting the turn after they are built (East/West Trading Post for raw materials from one neighbour, Marketplace for manufactured goods from both).
Dual-resource cards produce one OR the other resource per turn, not both; neighbours can buy either one.

Military resolution at the end of each Age: each player compares total Shields on their red cards (and Rhodes' Wonder) with each neighbour. Higher total takes a Victory token (+1 Age I, +3 Age II, +5 Age III); lower total takes a Defeat token (-1); equal gives nothing.
The game ends after the third Age (sixth turn of Age III) once Age III conflicts have been resolved and tokens distributed.
Military: sum all Victory and Defeat tokens (total can be negative).
Treasury: 1 victory point per set of 3 coins held at the end of the game.
Wonder: add the victory points shown on the built Wonder stages (e.g., side A: 3 for stage 1, 7 for stage 3, Giza stage 2 gives 5).
Civil buildings (blue cards): add the victory points printed on each.
Science (green cards), identical symbols: for each of the 3 symbols score the square of the number held (1 symbol=1, 2=4, 3=9, 4=16 points).
Science, sets: each group of 3 different symbols scores 7 points; this is added to the identical-symbol points.
Commercial buildings: certain Age III yellow cards give victory points at game end (e.g., Chamber of Commerce 2 points per grey card in own city).
Guilds (purple): each scores points based on the player's and/or neighbours' cities (e.g., Spies' Guild 1 point per red card in neighbouring cities).
The player with the highest total victory points wins.
In case of a tie, the tied player with the most coins in their treasury wins; a tie on coins is not broken.

Two-player expert variant: use the 3-player card set (3+ only), add a third 'Free City' Wonder board and the Border card between the players; each player gets 7 cards, the other 7 form a draw pile, and players and the Free City each start with 3 coins.

Two-player variant turn: the player holding the Free City card draws a card from the pile, picks one card for their own city then one for the Free City; the Free City discards for 3 coins only if it cannot play the card, and free chaining for it must be used. Players alternate holding the Free City card each turn.
Players may choose Wonder boards instead of random assignment, and side B boards (more complex but balanced) can be mixed with side A.
